entries.subject: DAMIT 5913: selected shape and spin
entries.finding: The official DAMIT metadata export was joined by model and asteroid identity and compared with the selected local recipe shape/model-5913.txt. Model 5913, version 2021-11-12, pole (28°, -17°), period 6.110939 h match the retained metadata. The archive diameter field is 144 ±3 km; its applicability to our scale is a separate calibration decision. This comparison checks source identity and metadata, not fresh mesh bytes, registration or the completeness of other archives.

entries.subject: AKARI thermal diameter as an alternative scale
entries.finding: [AKARI AcuA](https://data.darts.isas.jaxa.jp/pub/akari/AKARI-IRC_Catalogue_AllSky_AcuA_1.0/) — retained for comparison; the documented physical calibration supplies the selected scale. Its fitted nonrotating-sphere diameter is 160.61 ± 3.05 km. Formal catalog error omits additional shape, spin and thermal-model effects; no total confidence interval is invented. The original catalogue row for asteroid 173 was retrieved again and matched field-for-field with the retained row, including diameter, reported error and detection count.
entries.revisitWhen: A source-specific comparison with the selected shape and physical calibration justifies changing the adopted scale.

entries.subject: Registered surface imagery
entries.finding: No registered reflectance mosaic is supplied by this release; a neutral grid must mark unavailable imagery. Fine-scale craters, regolith and albedo are unresolved.
entries.revisitWhen: A released, reusable surface observation or mapped product with registration to this body’s selected source model; the existing grid alone does not imply that every archive was searched.

entries.subject: Shape and spin alternatives
entries.finding: The survey found no alternative archive solution for this target.
entries.revisitWhen: A released numerical replacement or independent pole/size constraints that distinguish the recorded alternatives, followed by comparison against the currently selected model.

entries.subject: Versioned browser evidence
entries.finding: The README records two browser cases before final integration, with an asset comparison to the integrated files, but no tested code revision for those cases. This is an evidence limitation, not proof of a current rendering defect.
entries.revisitWhen: A focused browser check identifies the tested revision, relevant served asset pins and capture settings, or the original report can be reliably bound to that revision and its dependencies.

entries.subject: VLT/SPHERE/ZIMPOL deconvolved frames as a computed-camera photograph lens
entries.finding: Measured with the cross-frame registration test on 25 deconvolved ZIMPOL frames (camera 1), each held against a reference built from the body's frames more than an hour away, cast through the ADAM reconstruction with the survey's rotation record read latitude-first. Disc interior 982 pixels (median); peak correlation 0.14 (median) against a mirror margin of 0.47; 0 of 25 frames decisive by the stated rule (peak at least 0.15 and margin at least 1.5), of which 0 peak within 5 degrees of the model. The frames carry no markings the test can register, so nothing in them confirms or refutes the rotation record's phase, pole or handedness; the silhouette gate that qualified Kleopatra cannot judge a body this round either. A photograph lens for this body would rest on the survey's record read by the route proven on Vesta and on five elongated bodies, with no check on this body itself; it is not derived until one exists.
entries.revisitWhen: A registration reference for this body: a spacecraft map, or frames in which the cross-frame test resolves markings (peak correlation above 0.15 with a mirror margin above 1.5 on most frames).
